cohort: The study involved 246 pregnant women at term gestation, categorized into a vaginal delivery group (n=128) and a caesarean section group (n=118).
finding: Vaginal delivery resulted in superior maternal recovery outcomes, reduced blood loss, shorter hospitalization, and earlier breastfeeding initiation compared to caesarean section, while neonatal Apgar scores remained comparable between groups.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery demonstrates superior maternal recovery outcomes, reduced blood loss, shorter hospitalization, and earlier breastfeeding initiation compared to caesarean section, while neonatal outcomes remain comparable when performed appropriately.
